newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds boosted by quick financing plan.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds boosted by quick financing plan.

text.p: Argentine bonds were flat to higher late Wednesday, supported by optimism in the government's quick debt financing early in the year.

Analysts said the announcement late Tuesday of the launch of a two-tranche $2.0 billion global bond and of another bond of $1.0 billion to be issued before the end of March lent support, considering most of Argentina's debt financing for 1997 will have been carried out after the placing of these two issues.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.10 to 123.65, while the FRB Brady bond due 2005 was flat at 86-3/8.

With these bond issues and $2.0 billion worth of bonds already sold in December covering 1997 spending needs, only $3.5 billion of the $8.5 billion in new debt slated for this year remains to be placed.
Still, "despite the firmness of the market, the bulk of investors are cautious and await the announcement of U.S. economic indicators that will be key for long-term U.S. rates," said a trader.
U.S. Treasuries turned lower in the afternoon in anticipation of the indicator releases and that cut the gains of Argentine bonds.
The United States will release December consumer and producer price inflation figures Thursday and December non-farm payrolls data Friday.
"There is general uncertainty on nervousness about U.S. rates," said another trader.
In the money markets, call money rates fell to 5.63 percent from 5.95 percent.
